sentences.text: Misc. Appeal No. 277 of 2016

Smt. Shardabai And Others
 Versus
 Vinod Kumar And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Vijay Singh Chouhan, learned counsel for the appella  Shri Sudarshan Pandit, learned counsel for the Respondent  ORDER I.A. No.5233/2021 is allowed for the reasons mentioned in it.
Heard finally.

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Accident Act, 1988 is preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 02.11.2015 in Claim Case No.218/2013 by 10th Additional Member of Motor Accident Claims, Tribunal, Indore for enhancement of Rs.4,00,000/-.

The facts of the case in short are as under:-
[2] An application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 was preferred seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of Nitin aged about 25 years in accident occurred on 27.04.2012 at 09:00 AM near Patel Dhaba, Balwada,
Aamroad, P.S. Balwada, District Khargone.
The Motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-09-NH-3516 dashed him by negligent manner which was riding by respondent No.1 and insured with the respondent No.2.
The deased was son of appellant No.1 and 2 and brother of appellant No.3 and 4.
He was bachelor.
He was earning Rs.8,000/- per month working in Ghanshyam Das & Company, Indore as a Supervisor.
He was also taking education.
[3] The claim application was contested by the respondent No.2/Insurance Company only.

[4] The Tribunal framed issue and recorded the evidence of Vishnu Prasad (PW-1), Neha (PW-2),
Sharad Kumar Behera, Account Assistant (PW-3) and Rupesh Yadav (PW-4) and admitted the documents Ex.P/1- to Ex.P/60.
[5] The Tribunal has partly allowed the claim case and awarded total compensation of Rs.6.66,515/-
alongwith interest @ 7 % from the date of application i.e.29.06.2012.

The aforesaid compensation Smt. Shardabai vs Vinod Kumar on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14501121/
1
Loss of Estate

Loss of dependency : Rs. 3,78,000/-
[6] This Misc. Appeal has been preferred on the ground that the future income has been assessed on lower side.
Future prospect has not been added.
Consortium has not been awarded.
[7] The Tribunal has estimated the age of Nitin/deceased as 25 years and assessed his income of Rs.3500/- per month.

Tribunal ought to have assessed Rs.4500/- per month and added 40% of increased in future prospect, calculating on that basis 50% for personal expenses, applied the multiplier of 18, loss of dependency comes to Rs.6,80,400/-.

The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.
3,78,000/-.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of dependency amount of Rs. 3,02,400/- is enhanced.
[8] No amount has been awarded in the head of loss of consortium, thus the appellant 1 and 2 are entitled to loss of consortium as Rs.80,000/-.
No amount has been awarded for the transportation during the treatment.
Accordingly, Rs.20,000/- is awarded in the head of transportation expenses.
The deceased was admitted in the Anand Hospital from 28.04.2012 to 18.05.2012 .
During period of treatment of deceased Nitin attended expenses of to the tune of Rs. 20,000/- is also awarded.

Accordingly, total compensation of Rs.3,02,400/- + 20,000/- + Rs.20,000/- total compensation of Rs.4,42,400/- (Rupees and same shall be carry 7 % interest with the date of filing of application i.e.
07.08.2012.

[9]. The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.4,00,000/- and paid the Court fee accordingly, however, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
With the above terms, Misc. Appeal is allowed and disposed of.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE Praveen Smt. Shardabai vs Vinod Kumar on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14501121/
